problems: E25 strengthens H1's HCT116 context link: the SRF ChIP-seq peak contains the variant. H1's statement that the evidence does not place the peak at the variant should be corrected.

E26 reports an HCT116 SP1 peak containing the variant, although its summit is 63 bp away. This supports local occupancy more directly than the prior evidence, but does not establish allele-specific binding at the exact base.
All five binding links rely on in-vitro family-screen predictions. None demonstrates allele-specific TF occupancy in HCT116 or that the predicted binding difference changes POU5F1B expression.

The alt T allele is the colorectal-cancer risk allele (E07) and is associated with increased POU5F1B expression in Colon Transverse (E06, E09). H3 and H5 predict greater binding to T, whereas H1 and H2 predict greater binding to G; without evidence for how each TF affects POU5F1B, these directions neither establish nor by themselves contradict a causal mechanism.

checks.why: Tests whether SRF has a ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in the proposed context, rather than only a reported HCT116 peak elsewhere.
Tests whether SP1 occupancy includes the variant in HCT116; this could strengthen or weaken the SP1 chain relative to SRF.
Tests for matched HNF4A occupancy at the variant, which is currently absent despite the strong alt-favoured family prediction.

critique.next_experiment: Use an allele-specific assay in HCT116 to test TF occupancy at the variant and the linked regulatory effect on POU5F1B—for example, allele-specific ChIP/CUT&RUN paired with an isogenic G-to-T edit and POU5F1B expression measurement. Prioritize SRF and SP1 given the matched-cell peaks, and include the other candidate factors if feasible.

lookups.why: Tests whether SRF has a ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in the proposed context, rather than only a reported HCT116 peak elsewhere.
Tests whether SP1 occupancy includes the variant in HCT116; this could strengthen or weaken the SP1 chain relative to SRF.
Tests for matched HNF4A occupancy at the variant, which is currently absent despite the strong alt-favoured family prediction.

games.reason: Both chains have ref-favoured in-vitro binding predictions and HCT116 ChIP peaks spanning the variant. A is more directly supported: SRF has its own mapped model predicting stronger binding to G, is expressed in HCT116, and an HCT116 SRF ChIP peak contains the variant. For B, the family model is SP4-based, and although SP1 is expressed and its peak spans the variant, its summit is 63 bp away. Neither chain establishes a causal TF-mediated effect on colorectal cancer.

Both predictions favor ref G, and both TFs are expressed in HCT116 with reported ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant. The SP1 summit is reported 63 bp away, but no comparable SRF summit distance is given, so the evidence does not establish that SRF is closer to the variant. The mapped SP4 model does not by itself count against SP1 under the stated rule. These records therefore do not separate the chains.
